record_reviews.summary: George’s multi-page phyllotaxy memorandum works through numbered spires, secondary spires and arithmetic progressions, with four preserved diagrams (A, B and related constructions). It also notes that CD’s letter containing information has not been found.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 11 May 1863], XML 1809-01-01 through 1863-05-10. The editorial relationship to the following letter gives a later research date; four diagrams were inspected as preserved visuals, but they add no date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George Howard Darwin is the writer; the diagrams and his calculations are his surviving work, while the referenced missing CD letter is not present.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 12746 is Darwin’s much later query about ripple rows in the Lime walk, not a phyllotaxy response; no date or distinctive calculation connects them.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The memorandum explicitly refers to a missing CD letter, but neither its text nor receipt date survives, so no response edge is proposed.

record_reviews.summary: George sends Darwin a draft letter for Nature correcting Darwin’s remarks on cirripede males and rudimentary structures, then asks about beef tea and discusses health and family logistics.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 3 October 1873], XML 1809-01-01 through 1873-10-02. The editorial note ties it to the 3 October 1873 letter and identifies a later Nature exchange.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George writes; the proposed Nature draft is an embedded document, and the scientific correction is George’s proposed publication rather than an 1847–1850 Darwin statement.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The draft responds to Darwin’s 20 September 1873 Nature letter, which is outside this period and absent from the packet; no period candidate exists.

record_reviews.summary: George reports that Cambridge plans to award Darwin an honorary LL.D. and asks how Darwin should refuse it; the university communication itself has not been found.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 28 May 1877], XML 1809-01-01 through 1877-05-27; the explicit Cambridge event is later and the upper bound alone cannot establish period eligibility.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George writes; the missing university letter is an institutional input, not a surviving source.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: A missing university approach is identified by the body, but no packet source or 1847–1850 date supports a link.

record_reviews.summary: George reports Kőrösi’s statistics on deaf-mutes and consanguinity, discusses a possible Nature article, and updates Darwin on Royal Society nominations and Hooker’s presidency.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 9 May 1878], XML 1809-01-01 through 1878-05-08. Editorial notes identify the 1878 correspondence and say no Nature article or letter on the deaf-children subject has been identified.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George writes; Kőrösi and Bőke are reported researchers, while the possible Nature article is an unlocated third-party/publication input.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The body itself records an unlocated article/letter, but no packet antecedent or period composition date is available.

record_reviews.summary: George discusses a Belgian Bulletin report and Lagrange’s alternative treatment of astronomical motions, explains his theoretical dynamics, and adds family news from Queen Anne Street.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 11 July 1878], XML 1809-01-01 through 1878-07-10. The cited 1877–78 Lagrange work and editorial relationship establish a later research context.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George writes; Lagrange’s paper and the Belgian report are external sources, not George’s own prior correspondence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The letter may answer an earlier George/Darwin exchange about Lagrange, but no specific incoming prompt survives and no period link is justified.

record_reviews.summary: George searches the London Library indexes for an 1802 Erasmus Darwin biography, reports references and says an enclosure is sent; the enclosure is not identified. The note may also answer Darwin’s request about Erasmus Darwin’s poem.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 3 May 1879], XML 1809-01-01 through 1879-05-02. Editorial notes tie it to the 1879 Erasmus Darwin publication and to the 3 May/5 May exchange, all later than 1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: George writes; the missing enclosure and possible earlier CD request are explicitly unlocated, so no text is attributed to them.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is a concrete missing-input boundary: the body identifies a sent but unavailable enclosure and a possible Darwin request, yet neither can be read or dated here.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks George whether flooded Lime-walk fruits arranged in transverse ripple rows reflect a mathematical pattern; the question is observational and narrowly addressed.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 9 October 1880], XML 1809-01-01 through 1880-10-08. Editorial notes point to George’s 1883 ripple-mark publication and a later November 1880 exchange; no 1847–1850 date is possible from the broad bound.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the later George publication is cited as editorial context, not a contemporaneous source.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 3887 is George’s 1863 phyllotaxy memorandum with numbered diagrams and a missing CD letter; 12746 concerns fruit ripple rows in 1880 and has no identifying overlap.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The question likely seeks George’s scientific answer, but no answer is in the packet and the later publication cannot be backdated.

issues: All records are boundary_date_probe items with only broad before-date upper bounds; packet membership does not establish 1847–1850 eligibility. Editorial bibliographies were read as apparatus and not treated as evidence of contemporary Darwin reading.
